title: Class 4 lies between class 2 and class 3 in activity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Class 4 lies between class 2 and class 3 in activity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although class 4 is the most complex in appearance, in terms of overall activity it is intermediate between class 2 and class 3, and in sequences of rules it commonly appears at the transition between class 2 and class 3 rules.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Class 4 systems are then in the middle: for the activity that they show neither dies out completely, as in class 2, nor remains at the high level seen in class 3.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Four Classes of Behavior” (from p. 231), p. 242. Scope: sequences of cellular automaton rules, both discrete and continuous

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Activity is directly measurable and parameterized continuous families allow clean transition tests. The assertion that this commonly holds across rule sequences remains dependent on how those sequences are chosen.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure asymptotic active-cell density and persistence across ordered parameterized rule sequences, then locate class 4 labels relative to transitions from localized periodic to extensive chaotic activity. Compare transition enrichment against randomized rule orderings.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite-time activity can be misleading.

There is no canonical ordering of discrete rules.

Class and transition labels are partly qualitative.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.94
analysis feasibility: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Activity is a direct time series, and the book's one-parameter sequences are fully specified, so the intermediate-activity pattern can be measured in days on those sequences. Commonly over sequences of rules, discrete and continuous, is wider than any one family, and class labels remain partly visual. The ordering is a real test on the published sequences and a sample beyond them.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define activity as the fraction of cells that change per step, assign classes by localized structures rather than by activity, and test whether class 4 sits between class 2 and class 3 along stated one-parameter rule sequences. A class 4 stretch whose activity matches class 3, or a sequence whose class 4 rules sit outside the class 2 to class 3 boundary, would challenge the claim in that family.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Commonly depends on how rule sequences are parametrized.

The ordering is informative only when class labels are not themselves activity thresholds.

A single class 4 run wavers, so the comparison needs a time average.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.75
